configs.description: CRS504-4XQ-IN - four 100G QSFP28 cages, a 100 Megabit management port with PoE in, an RJ45 console, a DC jack and a two-pin DC terminal, with two hot-swap AC supplies (part of the chassis in this model) and two fans. The box holds two power cords, rack ears and a fastening set.
configs.name: base

gaps.note: The dimensions drawing is filed as 04-4XQ-RMoutlineanddimensiondrawings_250851.pdf, with RM in the name, and its title block reads "504-4XQ-IN". The IN is the model with ears in the box and the two supply modules the drawing draws; no RM model exists on the product pages held. The drawing is used as the IN's.

The photograph prints "36 - 60 V" over the two DC inputs where the brochure and the quick guide say 36-57 V; the brochure's 43-57 V passive or 802.3bt class 6 PoE in is 42.5-57 V in the quick guide and passive 802.3af/at in the block diagram. The brochure's figures are carried and the legend is drawn as printed.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of the DC and PoE in ranges.

gaps.note: The brochure and the page print an operating temperature of -40 to +70 C; the quick guide's specification table prints 0 to +70 C. The brochure's is carried.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of the operating range.

gaps.note: The brochure calls the two power supplies hot-swap and prints no part number; no data sheet or drawing of the supply is held, and no document says what the box ships with or what covers an empty slot. They are drawn as part of the chassis with their inlets and no bay is added; the base configuration exports two AC power ports.
gaps.wanted: The supply's part number and a statement of what a slot holds when empty.

gaps.note: The drawing and photographs show a DC barrel jack, 10.3 x 11.9 mm, rated 36-57 V (brochure) and printed 36 - 60 V. It is the placed common/dc-barrel@1 (12 x 13 mm), which presents the dc-barrel interface the barrel plug mates, carrying the voltage and no current: no held document states a current or a barrel size for this jack. The part's own drawing of the socket stands in for the photographed one.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's current rating and barrel size for the DC jack.

gaps.note: The drawing and photographs show a two-pin pluggable DC terminal, 11.4 x 12.3 mm, beside the DC jack. It is the placed common/terminal-header-508-2@3 (12.16 x 8.6 mm), the two-position pluggable header the library already draws, which presents the terminal-508-2 interface a two-way plug mates. No held document states the terminal's pitch, so the 5.08 mm pitch of that part is an estimate: the drawing's 11.4 mm housing is about two positions of that pitch. The header is drawn empty and the photographed plug, 12.3 mm tall with its wire entries, is not drawn above it. The brochure lists the terminal as a DC input (36-57 V).
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of the terminal's pitch, or a drawing of the plug.

gaps.note: Searched the brochure, the page and the quick guide page for an LED table: none. The ACT and 100G lamps of each cage, the USER, FAULT and POWER lamps and the green lamp on each supply carry the component's own vocabulary and no meaning is stated. The lamps' resting colour comes from the lamp component and is not changed here: the photograph shows the bar lamps unlit grey and the render draws them with the component's own colour.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's LED description for the CRS504-4XQ-IN.

gaps.note: Photograph 2157 shows the two supply lamps lit green, the management link lamps lit green and yellow and the bar lamps mid grey, #838383. Every lamp is drawn at the lamp component's own resting colour, #3a3938, and no lit lamp is drawn; the photograph's lit and grey readings are recorded here and neither is chosen.
gaps.wanted: A statement of which state the photograph shows.

gaps.note: The QSFP28 cages, the console and management jacks and the C14 inlets are shared parts drawn for other boxes. Against photograph 2157 the cage frames are black with a silver edge and the jacks mid grey where the shared parts draw grey frames and light blue-grey jacks. The drawn parts are not changed here, because a new version of a shared part is a follow-up that moves other boxes' drawings.
gaps.wanted: A new version of each shared part drawn to these cages and jacks.

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The brochure lists "dual hot-swap power supplies" and 2 power cords; the quick guide lists 2 AC inputs at 100-240 V. The drawing and photographs show two modules at the front, each with a C14 inlet, a steel handle, a latch and a green lamp. No held document prints a part number for the supply, so none is named: the supplies are part of the chassis with their inlets, as on juniper/ex2300-24t, and there are no bays (gap `hot-swap-supplies`). No document says what covers an empty slot. The photograph prints "100-240 V 50/60 Hz" up the left edge of the first module and PSU 1 and PSU 2 beside them. The brochure's 41 W is the box's maximum power consumption and its 25 W the figure without attachments. Each module's handle is a steel bar 6.0 x 36 mm left of the inlet (read on the drawing's front view, 3.93 px per mm), its latch a 7.1 x 14.3 mm blue-grey grip at the module's left edge, and three screw holes sit in the face beside the modules; the legends are drawn at the size the drawing prints them (cap height 1.9 mm for the voltage run, 1.6 mm for PSU 1 and 2). Photograph 2158 shows two fan guards on the rear; the brochure and the page give no fan count and no fan statement.

chassis.note: 320 x 185 x 44, as the drawing prints them; the brochure and the page print 320 x 185 x 44 and agree. The drawing also dimensions 9 mm beyond the front (the two-pin terminal block), 8 mm beyond the rear (a stud) and 210 mm overall to the ends of the supply handles; none of these is part of the 185. The 481 mm across the ears is the ears' width, and the 462 mm the pitch of their holes.

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: product code CRS504-4XQ-IN, QCA9531 650 MHz MIPSBE, 64 MB RAM, 16 MB flash, 1 x 100M Ethernet, 4 x 100G QSFP28, switch chip 98DX4310, 320 x 185 x 44 mm, RouterOS v7 level 5, -40 to +70 C. Powering: three DC inputs (PoE-in 43-57 V passive or 802.3bt class 6; DC jack 36-57 V; 2-pin terminal 36-57 V), 25 W maximum without attachments and 41 W maximum. Included parts: 2 power cords, a fastening set, rack ears. The text says "dual hot-swap power supplies" and states no redundancy form. Each figure is filed as the document words it.

dc-inputs.note: Both DC inputs are placed parts: the jack as common/dc-barrel@1 and the terminal as common/terminal-header-508-2@3 (gaps `dc-jack` and `dc-terminal`). The jack is 10.3 x 11.9 mm at 289.8 mm, 25.4 mm down, a socket with a rim, a bore 5.6 mm across and a centre pin (photograph 2157 and the drawing). The two-pin pluggable terminal is 11.4 x 12.3 mm at 275.1 mm, 25.1 mm down: a cap 10.0 x 4.1 mm over a housing 11.4 x 8.2 mm with two wire entries, measured on the drawing's front view at 3.94 px per mm (the housing from x 1799.4 to 1844.4 px and y 536 to 584.4 px of the page image, body corner at 715.5, 437), and the drawing dimensions it 9 mm proud of the front; it is drawn flat. That agrees with the CRS510 drawing's reading of the same terminal (11.4 x 11.8 at 275.4 mm); the first reading of 9.4 x 9.8 mm for this model took the housing without its cap and the jack at 9.0 x 10.8 mm too small. The registry's common/dc-terminal-plug-2 is a 32.1 x 17.6 mm part drawn for another maker's box, so the two-position header common/terminal-header-508-2@3 is placed instead (gap `dc-terminal`). The metal prints "36 - 60 V" over both inputs (the dash is not resolved in photograph 2157, which reads "36   60 V"; the drawing prints a dash); the brochure and the quick guide say 36-57 V (gap `power-figures`). A bracket spans both inputs; the terminal's two marks, left to right, are a circled minus and a circled plus; the jack's are a circled minus, a pin symbol with its dot joined by a line to the circled plus: the centre pin is the positive pole, as read from the photograph.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (the brochure and the page: Rack ears). The drawing's front view draws them 80.5 mm either side of the 320 mm body (481 mm over the ears, holes 462 mm apart). They are shipped flush with the face and are not drawn on it; no `at` is written and no kit is listed.

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Two supply modules 52.6 x 38.2 mm at 12.2 and 72.1 mm, 2.3 mm down, each with a C14 inlet turned a quarter turn (18 wide by 25 tall, earth pin at the left) centred 50.2 and 110.2 mm and 24.9 mm down, a green lamp, a six-slot vent and a latch. Four QSFP28 cages 20.6 mm wide and 10.9 mm tall, measured on the pixels at 144.9, 171.1, 197.3 and 223.3 mm (a 26.1 mm pitch) and 26.1 mm down, with a bracket and the cage number over each and two lamps under each. A woven slot vent 97.7 x 11.5 mm over the cages. The console and management jacks share a plate 18.1 x 26.8 at 248.6 mm, 10.6 mm, the console above. RESET is a ring at 271.9 mm, 34.6 mm. The two-pin terminal is 11.4 x 12.3 mm at 275.1 mm and the DC jack housing 10.3 x 11.9 mm at 289.8 mm. Three lamps are small bars under the jacks.

gate-1.note: The drawing's front view body is 1255 px wide between its left and right lip lines for the printed 320 mm (3.92 px per mm in the page image) and 44 mm tall, the printed 44. Every x and y below is taken at 3.93 px per mm from the body's top-left corner of the front view; cage edges were measured on the pixels (about 0.3 mm), the other features read off a 3 times enlargement of the view (about 0.7 mm).

lamps.note: Each cage has two bar lamps under it, printed ACT at the left and 100G at the right (photograph 2157), centred 7.95 mm either side of the cage centre. The three bar lamps at the right are printed USER, FAULT and POWER. The green lamp on each supply module is drawn as the photograph shows it. No document says what a lamp shows (gap `led-states`).

management-and-console.note: Photograph 2157 prints CONSOLE over the upper jack and MGMT/PoE in under the lower. The page counts one 100M Ethernet port, the management port, filed at 100m; the brochure lists PoE in at 43-57 V passive or 802.3bt class 6 on it, which is an input and is carried in the power attributes, not as a PoE out. The block diagram says 43-57 V, passive, 802.3af/at.

port-numbering.note: The metal prints 1 2 3 4 over the cages on a bracket, left to right.

rear-layout.note: Photograph 2158 (2216 x 1279 px) looks at the rear, the 320 mm face, not at a wall. The lid's long edge above the guards and the short edge along the face that carries the ear's four-hole flange stand in 1.7 to 1 (the lid is 320 x 185); the lid's slots run parallel to that short face and the CLOUD SWITCH lettering runs along the guard face, upside down and at the far edge; the earthing stud shows at the left end of the guard face, which is the end the drawing's top plan puts it at, seen from behind. The face's four corners in the photograph (151,400 upper left, 1050,931 upper right, 1052,1126 lower right and 171,560 lower left, as seen from behind) were transformed onto 320 x 44 mm at 10 px per mm. The transform reads the guards' rings 36.8 mm wide and 40.8 mm tall, the screw-hole recesses 1.09 and the hexagon cells about 1.1 taller than their width (a regular cell reads 1.155 across the corners over the flats; these read 1.06 to 1.1): the face's corners pin its length at 320 mm, so the stretch is taken in the height, and heights are divided by 1.09 about the face's middle (the stud's base then reads 10.5 mm from the left end, the drawing's 11.0, and 34.1 mm down, the drawing's 9.2 mm up from the bottom, 34.8). Each guard is drawn round, 37.0 mm across (the corrected height reads 37.4; no held source shows an oval), centred 114.8 and 154.8 mm from the stud's end and 22.0 mm down, 40.0 mm apart, round a clear hub 21.0 mm across in the face's colour (#d4d4d4; the hub and the plain face both read #bababa in the shaded photograph, box 1100,190 to 1200,260 with 7000 pixels and box 2200,100 to 2600,300 with 80000 pixels of the transformed image). The hexagon cells are 6.3 mm apart in a column (66 px), so the renderer's tile 8.86 x 5.11 mm is scaled by 1.233 on both axes to 10.92 x 6.3 mm (the first drawing used the base tile unscaled; its holes then read 5.1 mm across the corners where the photograph's cells, walls included, are about 6 mm; the vertical reading is 6.05 mm after the division and the diagonal one 6.6, hence 6.3); a cell sits on each ring's centre (the left column of cells reads 15.5 mm from the centre, three columns of 5.46 mm, and half a row up); about seven columns run across a ring. Each guard has a screw hole at its upper right and its lower left, as seen from behind, 3.8 mm across, centred 15.4 to 18.2 mm along and 15.5 to 16.6 mm across from the ring's centre; the fill #232323 is the median of 224 pixels of the dark opening (box 1320,36 to 1334,52 of the transformed image) and the lighter recess round it is not drawn. The cell width, the guards' height and the holes are estimated to about 2 mm. The left wall's two holes are read from the drawing's end view, at 3.94 px per mm (page image, wall from x 2494 to 2668 px, rear end at y 928, rings centred at 2585,947.7 and 2604.7,947.7): the view is the left wall, seen from outside with the front at the bottom of the page, because it puts the stud 9.1 mm from the edge that photograph 2158 shows is the bottom, so the lid is at the right of the page; its two rings are 2.8 mm across, 5.0 mm from the rear end and 15.9 and 20.9 mm below the lid, and 2158's left wall shows the same two dots near its rear end. They are drawn 5.0 mm in from the left wall's rear edge (that face's x runs from the rear). Their fill #646464 is the median of two boxes of 64 pixels (2158, boxes 1070,986 to 1078,994 and 1069,1010 to 1077,1018) of the same holes, estimated, as the drawing has no colour. The right wall is not drawn: no held document shows it (gap `right-wall`).

sources.note: Dimensions drawing, MikroTik, title block "504-4XQ-IN", "Printed: 02.10.2023" (file 04-4XQ-RMoutlineanddimensiondrawings_250851.pdf: the file name says RM, the title block says IN; page image at 3308 px across, 3.93 px per mm on the front view): front with the ears, top plan and end view. It is the IN's: the front view draws the IN's two AC supply modules, four QSFP28 cages, console and management jacks, DC terminal block and DC jack, and rack ears, its 320 x 185 x 44 mm agrees with the IN's brochure and page, and it shows nothing of the -OUT (whose page describes an IP66 weatherproof enclosure with hose clamps). CRS504-4XQ-IN brochure, MikroTik (file CRS504-4XQ-IN_220440.pdf; no date is printed, the file name carries a revision stamp): specifications, powering and included parts. Product page, MikroTik (https://mikrotik.com/product/crs504_4xq_in, saved 2026-10-26). Declaration of conformity ID-209.1 (file ID209.1_CRS504_4XQ_IN_DOC_231003.pdf, Riga, 17 October 2023): names the model and pictures it, says nothing of the drawing and holds no dimension. Studio photographs: 2156 (front, three-quarter from the left, above), 2157 (front, from slightly above), 2158 (front right and the right wall, from above), 2159 (front, three-quarter, with the ears), 2160 (front, from slightly above, with the ears), 2161 (a three-quarter that lies the unit on its side, showing the lid), 2162 (the block diagram) and 2163 (an application diagram); all show the IN. The quick guide page (Quick Guide - CRS504-4XQ-IN, help.mikrotik.com, last updated Jun 30, 2025) holds no figure and no LED table. The block diagram CRS504-4XQ-INr3_261029.png. NetBox's device type as a second opinion only. MikroTik prints no figure numbers. The hardware manual page is not held.

vents.note: The cage vent is a woven field of slots at about plus and minus 45 degrees with small diamond holes (squares turned 45 degrees, 1.6 mm across, one at each edge of the band, as photograph 2157 and the drawing show them), drawn as a `motif` tile 16.9 x 11.5 mm (the existing patterns draw no slanted slots) over a field 97.0 x 11.5 mm (the drawing's 97.7 trimmed by 0.7 mm so that the cut at the right end, 12.5 mm into the last period, leaves no sliver of a slot), 5.74 periods, the field starting at the tile's left edge with square corners. Read off photograph 2157 at 4.953 px per mm (the face's 1585 px for 320 mm): the period is 83.5 px (16.86 mm) from four periods of the long slot, 16.9 here (estimated). The photograph looks down on the face, whose 44 mm height reads 184 px (4.18 px per mm, 0.84 of the horizontal scale), and the band reads 43.5 px tall, 9.0 mm at the face's vertical scale against the drawing's 11.5 mm: the photograph is foreshortened, the drawing is orthographic and wins for the field's size, and the weave is stretched vertically to it (the long slot reads 41.1 degrees in the photograph and 47.8 after). The drawing's front view is too small to read the weave. The supply vents are rects of slots measured on the drawing's front view of the first supply (3.94 px per mm; the drawing draws both alike, so the second is offset by the 59.9 mm between the modules): two rows of three slots 3.9 x 7.8 mm and four slots in the top row.
